new.description: The single integration crate cargo auto-discovers from `tests/it/main.rs`: main.rs declares `mod common;` once plus one `mod <name>;` per moved suite; each moved `tests/<name>.rs` lands at `tests/it/<name>.rs` with its `mod common;` line rewritten to `use crate::common;`; `tests/common/mod.rs` moves to `tests/it/common/mod.rs` (its header paragraph documents the per-binary recompilation its blanket `allow(dead_code)` exists to absorb — rewrite it, and narrow the allow, once one crate unifies dead-code analysis). `tests/fixtures/` does NOT move: `common::fixture` resolves it from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` + `tests/fixtures`, so that join stands unchanged. The 15 live snapshots re-bless under `tests/it/snapshots/` — insta keys the filename off the module path, so the new names are insta's to write and never hand-predicted; the two `adapter_fidelity__*.snap` in the retire list are orphans of the already-retired `tests/adapter_fidelity.rs` (`tests/memory_contract.rs:6` records the retirement) and are swept by this move rather than carried across — re-blessing regenerates only referenced snapshots.

edit.description: An explicit `[[test]] name = "it"` target only if auto-discovery of `tests/it/main.rs` needs it. `autotests` stays on: with it off, a later stray `tests/foo.rs` compiles into no target and its tests silently never run — a vacuous green, the failure mode engineering.md's 'A green verdict is proven non-vacuous' names.

summary: The suite declares 59 integration-test targets, so `tests/common` is one home in source and 55 linked copies in target/ — fold them into one `tests/it` crate.

tests.asserts: the snapshot-heaviest suite passes byte-identical assertions after re-blessing under tests/it/snapshots/ — the moved suites assert exactly what they asserted before
every one of the 59 moved suites is declared as a module, so the consolidated run's test count equals the 59-target run's — a suite missing from main.rs is a suite that silently stops running

acceptance: `cargo test` green with a test count equal to the pre-move run's (capture it before the move and compare, so no suite is lost in the fold), `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` green over the single crate, and one integration-test executable in target/debug/deps where 59 stood — the decidable pin, per the cost section's 'The pin is a count, never a clock'. The commit body reports `cargo test --no-run` wall time and peak RSS before and after, timing staying the manual signal a human reads rather than a gate; that pair is also what answers the standing objection, that one crate compiles as one unit, so peak RSS falls while wall time may rise.
